59183065.b:
Download the brochure

Under the banner "AlUla Moments," more than 50 events across 4 festivals begin in AlUla Governorate on 21 December and continue until 30 March. They are: the famous Winter at Tantora, returning to great public welcome and celebrating heritage; AlUla Skies; AlUla Arts; and a festival of wellness and relaxation. Concerts also return to Maraya Concert Hall, which will again lead the cultural scene as a venue for regional and international performances starting next October.

Winter at Tantora

Winter at Tantora, the Kingdom's first music and arts festival, returns for 6 weeks with a new look and design. The festival opens with a magical orchestral performance by candlelight at Hegra, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, marking the start of the festival season in AlUla.

The equestrian events include the long-awaited fashion show, the horsemen's fashion show at Ekmah; the return of the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques Endurance Cup (Horsemen's Gathering); the AlUla Desert Polo Championship; and the AlUla Citrus Festival. The Harrat Uwayrid viewpoint, connected to the neighboring restaurant Back to Black, offers stunning views of sunrise and sunset in AlUla from the top of Harrat Uwayrid. Cultural and archaeological workshops are held at heritage sites, and interactive shows return to AlUla Old Town and AlUla Oasis. Winter at Tantora runs from 21 December to 12 February.

AlUla Arts

Starting in February 2021, the AlUla Arts Festival hosts art exhibitions and a variety of gatherings with many artistic talents, celebrating AlUla's rich heritage as a historic center and meeting point for cultural exchange. The award-winning Maraya hall also hosts the "Art of Our Time" exhibition, which presents the latest contemporary works by prominent artists from the Kingdom. Al Jadidah will be a lively hub for art activity and varied performances, with the open-air Hosh Cinema showing films by local Saudi filmmakers, as well as curated artistic experiences inspired by the culture and heritage of the oasis and other parts of the governorate. The AlUla Arts Festival is held from 13 February, with exhibitions and events continuing until the end of March.

AlUla Skies

AlUla's many captivating geological landscapes, from volcanic plains to ancient heritage sites, are best seen from the air during the AlUla Skies festival.

The new Constellations show, a high-tech sound and light experience, adds to visitors' stargazing in AlUla, while "Symphony Under the Stars" lets visitors enjoy a stunning musical performance under millions of twinkling stars. All of this is available for booking from 27 February to 12 March.

Building on its history as a place of rest and recreation, the AlUla Cultural Oasis will become a destination for calm and relaxation from this coming December. The "Garden of Moments" activity offers an amazing experience in an environment that responds to space, light, and sound, with installations that stimulate the imagination.

Wellness and Relaxation

As part of the AlUla Wellness Festival in March 2022, the Sanctuary of the Five Senses brand will offer a complete range of mind, body, and spirit experiences led by yoga and meditation practitioners.

For more energetic activities, Eco Trail returns to AlUla with exercise sessions in AlUla Oasis, offering daily doses of endorphins in group fitness classes.

This year the "Sand-Immersed Sessions" around Elephant Rock also return, with new adventure experiences.

Festival calendar:

Winter at Tantora: 21 December to 12 February.

AlUla Arts: 13 February to 26 February.

AlUla Skies: 27 February to 12 March.

AlUla Wellness and Relaxation: 17-27 March.

Facts and figures:

The 2021/2022 events calendar includes more than 50 events across 4 unique festivals.

8 main events will anchor the festivals' themes.

30 permanent attractions will remain in AlUla.

Performances will feature 5 of the region's top artists and 3 major international names.

2.9 billion will be added to AlUla's gross domestic product.

600 jobs will be created.

6 small and medium-sized enterprises will be supported.

59092134.s: Al Masmak Fortress is one of the most prominent historic landmarks in Ad Dirah District in central Riyadh, and one of the few buildings still standing since the city's founding. It was built in 1282 AH (1865 CE) during the reign of Imam Abdullah bin Faisal bin Turki to protect the city, and is notable for its sturdy walls and small openings for rifle barrels, with only two main entrances.
59092134.b:
Al Masmak Fortress is one of the most prominent historic landmarks in Ad Dirah District in central Riyadh, and one of the few buildings still standing since the city's founding. It was built in 1282 AH (1865 CE) during the reign of Imam Abdullah bin Faisal bin Turki to protect the city, and is notable for its sturdy walls and small openings for rifle barrels, with only two main entrances.

In 1319 AH (1902 CE), King Abdulaziz Al Saud recaptured the fortress during the battle to retake Riyadh. It was later used as an ammunition store and then a prison, before being converted into a museum documenting the story of the recapture of Riyadh and the journey of the Kingdom's unification. The museum was officially opened on 11 June 1995 to present the stages of the Kingdom's founding under the founding King, may God rest his soul.

59091829.s: Mount Tuwaiq is one of the most important geographical landmarks in the Arabian Peninsula and one of the most prominent topographical features visible from outer space. It is the heart of the historic Al Yamamah region and of the Najd region.
59091829.b:
Mount Tuwaiq is one of the most important geographical landmarks in the Arabian Peninsula and one of the most prominent topographical features visible from outer space. It is the heart of the historic Al Yamamah region and of the Najd region.

The name Tuwaiq is a diminutive of the word "tawq" (collar), and using diminutives to make names sound pleasing was an old Arab custom. Tuwaiq is one of the oldest landmarks in Najd, known to the peoples of the Arabian Peninsula for a very long time. International archaeological excavations under way today, supervised by the Saudi Commission for Tourism and National Heritage, reach deep into prehistory, revealing many exciting details about ancient human migrations and confirming the existence of ancient villages along the Tuwaiq Mountains.
